title: Common carotid artery is a third aortic arch derivative
vignette: A 64-year-old man loses consciousness near the entrance to an emergency room. A physician rushes to the patient and palpates a strong pulse along the inner side of the left sternocleidomastoid muscle. The vessel palpated by the doctor is a derivative of which of the following aortic arches?

clues.text: palpates a strong pulse along the inner side of the left sternocleidomastoid muscle
clues.note: A pulse along the medial (inner) border of the sternocleidomastoid is the carotid pulse - specifically the common carotid artery, whose embryologic origin is being asked.

whatMatters: The pulse along the medial border of the sternocleidomastoid is the COMMON CAROTID artery. The common carotid and the proximal internal carotid derive from the THIRD aortic arch. Answer C.
strategy: Identify the vessel (common carotid) from its landmark, then recall the aortic arch derivatives. Third arch = common carotid + proximal internal carotid ('C is 3rd letter - Carotid'). Reject first (maxillary artery), second (stapedial/hyoid), fourth (aortic arch on left, proximal right subclavian), and sixth (pulmonary arteries + ductus arteriosus).

eliminations.label: First arch - maxillary artery
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the first aortic arch gives rise to a portion of the maxillary artery. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: that is not the common carotid. ✅ Correct if: asking about the maxillary artery (first arch).

eliminations.label: Second arch - stapedial/hyoid artery
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the second aortic arch forms the stapedial and hyoid arteries (largely regress). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: not the common carotid. ✅ Correct if: asking about the stapedial artery (second arch).

eliminations.label: Fourth arch - aortic arch / proximal subclavian
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the fourth arch forms the true aortic arch (left) and the proximal right subclavian artery. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the common carotid is a THIRD-arch derivative, not fourth. ✅ Correct if: asking about the aortic arch or proximal right subclavian.

eliminations.label: Sixth arch - pulmonary arteries / ductus arteriosus
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the sixth arch forms the proximal pulmonary arteries and (on the left) the ductus arteriosus. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: unrelated to the carotid. ✅ Correct if: asking about pulmonary arteries or the ductus arteriosus.

reasoning: A pulse along the medial border of the sternocleidomastoid = the common carotid artery
Aortic arch derivatives: 3rd arch -> common carotid + proximal internal carotid
mechanism: During development, the pharyngeal (aortic) arches give rise to specific arterial derivatives. The THIRD aortic arch forms the common carotid artery and the proximal part of the internal carotid artery (the third arch also relates to the glossopharyngeal nerve, CN IX). The common carotid ascends deep to the medial border of the sternocleidomastoid, where its pulse is palpable and where it bifurcates into internal and external carotid arteries. A useful mnemonic: the aortic arch derivatives are 1st = part of the maxillary artery, 2nd = stapedial/hyoid, 3rd = Common Carotid + proximal internal Carotid ('C' is the third letter), 4th = aortic arch (left) and proximal right subClavian ('4th = systemiC/aortiC'), and 6th = pulmonary arteries and (left) ductus arteriosus. Thus the palpated common carotid is a third-arch derivative.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Embryo > aortic arch derivatives: 1st maxillary, 2nd stapedial/hyoid, 3rd common + proximal internal carotid, 4th aortic arch/proximal right subclavian, 6th pulmonary arteries + ductus arteriosus.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Recognize the carotid pulse (medial to sternocleidomastoid) and map the common carotid to the third arch.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on aortic (pharyngeal) arches, common vs internal carotid, or the arch derivative mnemonic? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: 1st = maxillary, 2nd = stapedial, 4th = aortic arch/subclavian, 6th = pulmonary/ductus - none is the common carotid.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: 3rd aortic arch = common carotid + proximal internal carotid ('C' = 3rd letter).
